definition: D–KEFS, in this packet, refers to the Delis-Kaplan Executive Function System Sorting Test, a neuropsychological assessment used to examine executive functions. It is used to add information about abilities such as abstract and conceptual reasoning, beyond tests that mainly measure memory, attention, and processing speed.

reasons: The packet supports the Delis-Kaplan Executive Function System Sorting Test (D-KEFS ST), not D–KEFS as the sorting test itself; the acronym/sense is therefore incorrect.

The definition should not generalize beyond the packet’s specific use in this article, which concerns a particular sorting test added to a broader neuropsychological battery rather than D–KEFS in general.

The packet does not support the specific claim that D–KEFS “adds information about abilities such as abstract and conceptual reasoning” (it states BRB-NT mainly assesses memory/attention/processing speed and does not properly investigate executive functions, and separately notes that failures in abstract and conceptual reasoning can occur, but it does not link that example to D–KEFS ST specifically).
